subject: Math
prompt: Line $s$ is defined by $y = \frac{(13)}{9} x + 6$. Line $t$ is parallel to line $s$ in the xy-plane. What is the slope of line $t$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. For an equation written in the form $y = m x + b$, $m$ is the slope and $b$ is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept. The given equation $y = \frac{13}{9} x + 6$ has slope $\frac{13}{9}$, so line $s$ has slope $\frac{13}{9}$. Since parallel lines have equal slopes, line $t$ also has slope $\frac{13}{9}$.
